sections.html:
Fort Lee is mostly towers, so a quick sale usually involves the borough's Certificate of Compliance for sales, any association paperwork and, for rented units, rent leveling records. Only 55.4 percent of homes are owner-occupied, which leaves close to half in the hands of renters.

The borough sits on the Hudson Palisades at the eastern edge of Bergen County, right at the western end of the George Washington Bridge. It covers 2.87 square miles, 12.33 percent of it water, and had 40,191 residents in 2020 and an estimated 40,345 in 2025. That works out to about 15,960 people per square mile of land. Apartment construction along Palisade Avenue and Boulevard East began in the 1960s, so most inventory dates from after 1960 and sits under an association or a management company.

Rents are high and the commute is long. These are 2020 to 2024 estimates.

There are 18,287 households averaging 2.19 people. A price near the median value lands in the $200,000 to $550,000 transfer fee band described under closing costs.

sections.h2: What paperwork does Fort Lee ask of sellers?
sections.html:
The borough issues its own Certificate of Compliance for sales through the Fire Prevention Bureau, and its forms page offers a separate version for rentals. Ask the bureau for the current packet, the inspection fee and the earliest appointment before you fix a closing date.

Other borough forms a seller or landlord may need:

  • A subcode application for a certificate through the Building Department.
  • A sidewalk permit application, if the frontage needs repair.
  • Rent leveling registration for newly rented apartments, and a separate form for a newly rented condo, co-op or one-family home.
  • A landlord identity registration form for rent leveling.
  • A tax assessor property record search and deduction forms for senior, disabled and veteran owners.

Fort Lee also has a Parking Authority that issues residential parking permits, so tell a buyer who will not have a garage how permit parking works.

Selling a unit in a tower can add association steps before the deed passes. Ask the board or management office what it requires from a seller, whether it issues a resale package, and whether a co-op buyer needs board approval. Make that request at the start, before a contract is signed, so the closing date reflects the association's timetable.

The state classifies co-ops as Class 4C property, and the Division of Taxation applies the graduated percent fee to them on deeds above $1 million. It starts at 1 percent of the total price for sales between $1,000,000 and $2,000,000 and rises in steps to 3.5 percent above $3.5 million. The seller is responsible for it.

sections.h2: How do Fort Lee's roads and transit affect buyers?
sections.html:
Position at the George Washington Bridge shapes how buyers judge a property. The bridge, signed as I-95, U.S. 1-9 and U.S. 46, carries traffic into Washington Heights in Upper Manhattan. Other roads through the borough include Route 4, Route 5, Route 67, U.S. 9W, County Route 505 and the Palisades Interstate Parkway.

  • NJ Transit buses 154, 156, 158 and 159 go to the Port Authority Bus Terminal in Midtown.
  • NJ Transit routes 171, 175, 178, 181, 182, 186 and 188 go to the George Washington Bridge Bus Terminal.
  • Rockland Coaches runs along Route 9W to Port Authority and the bridge terminal.

With a mean commute of 35 minutes, well above the national 26.4, buyers will ask how close a building is to a bus stop. Neighborhood names to use in a listing include Coytesville, Linwood, Palisade and Taylorville, along with the Palisade Avenue and Boulevard East tower corridor and downtown Main Street.

The seller pays the state Realty Transfer Fee, which is based on the price written in the deed. On a sale over $350,000, the band from $200,000 to $550,000 is $4.80 per $500, which is where a price near Fort Lee's $448,000 median value lands. The deed, the fee and the Gross Income Tax form are filed with the Bergen County Clerk.

Corporations, partnerships and multi-member LLCs file a GIT/REP-3 and check Box 5, and so do single-member LLCs. Individual sellers who live outside New Jersey owe an estimated payment of at least 2 percent of the price, or the gain times 10.75 percent if that is higher, unless the form's assurances apply. The state GIT/REP Unit answers questions at 609-322-9275.

For assessment disputes, call the Bergen County Board of Taxation at 201-336-6300 to confirm the current appeal deadline.

sections.h2: Steps for a quick Fort Lee sale
sections.html:
Start with the building. Ask the management office for the resale package and any board approval steps, and ask Fire Prevention for the Certificate of Compliance packet. If the unit is rented, pull the rent leveling registration and give the buyer copies. Then have your closing attorney prepare the deed and the transfer fee and GIT/REP filings, which go to the Bergen County Clerk at recording.

A cash buyer can often skip a mortgage appraisal timeline, but the borough certificate and any association approval still set the pace.

Bring a short folder to your attorney: the deed, your latest tax bill, a mortgage payoff statement, the association's contact details and, for a rental, the lease and deposit figure. If the frontage has a cracked or failed sidewalk, file the sidewalk permit application early so the repair does not hold up the certificate. A seller who lives outside New Jersey should also ask the attorney about the estimated Gross Income Tax payment well before the closing date, since it is collected at the table.

An owner who is an LLC or other entity should confirm which GIT/REP box applies before the closing date, because a wrong form can get the deed rejected at recording. The county clerk makes the final call on whether to accept a deed, so a questioned filing is better settled early than on the morning of closing.

faqs.q: Does Fort Lee require a certificate to sell a home?
faqs.a: Yes. The borough issues a Certificate of Compliance for sales through its Fire Prevention Bureau, and the packet is on the borough's forms page. Ask the bureau for the fee and inspection schedule before you set a closing date.

faqs.q: Are Fort Lee rentals subject to rent leveling?
faqs.a: Fort Lee has a rent leveling office with registration forms for newly rented apartments and for newly rented condo, co-op or one-family units. Landlords should confirm their registrations are current and give the buyer copies. The rent leveling office can explain the current rules.

faqs.q: What is the mansion tax on a Fort Lee condo sale?
faqs.a: It is the graduated percent fee on deeds above $1 million, and the seller pays it. It starts at 1 percent for sales up to $2 million and reaches 3.5 percent above $3.5 million. It applies to Class 2 residential and Class 4C cooperative units.

faqs.q: How does an LLC sign the seller form in Fort Lee?
faqs.a: An LLC files the GIT/REP-3 and checks Box 5, which covers sellers that are not individuals, estates or trusts. Single-member LLCs follow the same instruction.

faqs.q: Which county office records a Fort Lee deed?
faqs.a: The Bergen County Clerk. The state Realty Transfer Fee and the Gross Income Tax form are filed with the deed, and your closing attorney or title company handles the submission and confirms the fee.
